check: uninstall safety: does the mod leave anything behind in a world
question: The mod registers persistent chunk attachments. Persistent means written into saved chunks, which normally raises the question of what happens if the mod is later removed.
answer: Nothing is written, so there is nothing to leave behind.
chain: ProductionSession's constructor requires all of: greatwall.s1c.productionFixture=true, greatwall.production unset, a file named greatwall_s1c_fixture in the game directory, and a file named greatwall_test_world. Any real client fails all four, so it throws rather than proceeding.
The other construction site, WorldServices:208, only builds a WallStageCoordinator when greatwall.s0.terrain is set.
Those two sites are the only ones, and WallStageCoordinator is the only thing that ever calls setAttached on the two persistent attachments.
whyPersistentIsStillCorrect: createPersistent is the right choice for the code that does use it: those attachments must survive ProtoChunk promotion and serialization, as the class doc says. The property is only risky if something writes them, and nothing does without the flags.
noBlocksOrItems: No Registry.register for BLOCK or ITEM exists anywhere in src/main, so there is no content id that a save could reference and then fail to resolve.
conclusion: Installing and later removing the jar leaves no residue: no block or item ids to dangle and no attachment ever written.
